today_items.name: TSK Thesis guidelines check: TPP + Institute-wide (before Overleaf)
today_items.agenda:
Read the rules BEFORE creating the document, so the Overleaf file is right from the first commit rather than reformatted in January.

TWO LAYERS, and they are different documents:

1. INSTITUTE-WIDE (MIT Libraries, binding on everyone)
   libraries.mit.edu/distinctive-collections/thesis-specs/
   Key points already confirmed:
     - Title page is ALWAYS page 1; every page counted in one consecutive sequence including prefatory material, figures, appendices.
     - Abstract: 500 words or less, single-spaced, immediately after the title page. Avoid formulas/special characters.
     - Body may be single, 1.5, or double spaced. Abstract, biography, notes, bibliography, acknowledgements are single-spaced.
     - NO signature page in the final document - but your DEPARTMENT may require a separate one.
     - Sans serif font suggested (not required) for readability.
     - Degree conferral date must read February, May/June, or September only.
     - Title page and abstract must MATCH the metadata you submit to the Libraries exactly.
   Spec was revised April 2026 - read the current version, not a cached PDF.

2. DEPARTMENT (TPP and AeroAstro - you are dual, so check BOTH)
   Ask each program office directly. Departments set their own committee composition, signature page, internal deadlines, and page/chapter conventions, and the Institute page does not cover these.
   For a DUAL degree the Libraries publish a specific sample title page: 'Dual degree with extra committee members'. Use that one, not the standard example.

QUESTIONS TO GET ANSWERED IN WRITING:
  - Does TPP have its own thesis format guide or internal deadline earlier than 12 Dec?
  - For the dual degree, do BOTH departments sign, and how many readers total?
  - Does either department require a separate signature page?
  - Is there a TPP-specific abstract or policy-content requirement?

Contacts: mit-theses@mit.edu for Institute questions. Barb / Rachael for TPP. AeroAstro grad office for 16.

today_items.name: TSK Stationery run: Harvard Square, MUJI and Bob Slate
today_items.location: 48 Brattle St and 30 Brattle St, Cambridge
today_items.notes: BIGGEST WIN IS PAPER, not pens. Printing packets on 24 lb / 90 gsm instead of standard 20 lb stops gel ink ghosting through the page. Hammermill Premium Multipurpose 24 lb, 97 bright, 500 sheets, rated for BOTH inkjet and laser so it is fuser safe. Staples SKU 166140. Check the shelf price in store: the listing showed 38.99 which looks like a multi ream pack, single reams run about 14. Never put coated or glossy paper through a laser printer. ROUTE: Red Line Kendall to Harvard, 2 stops. MUJI 48 Brattle and Bob Slate 30 Brattle are 100 feet apart. Blick at 619 Massachusetts Ave is walkable from MIT and stocks Zebra, Uni and Pentel. Staples or the Coop for paper and the binder. AT MUJI: gel ink pens 0.38 and 0.5 black, aluminium ruler, clear folders, pen case. AT BOB SLATE: handle the Japanese notebooks, Maruman, Kokuyo, Midori. Paper feel is the reason to come in person. Closes 1800 Thursday. BINDER: US Letter 1 inch 3 ring plus a 3 hole punch, Staples or Coop, about 15 dollars. NOT MUJI: Japanese binders are A4 with 26 or 30 holes and will not fit. ONLINE at jetpens.com, free shipping over 35 dollars, about 33 dollars total: Uni-ball Signo RT1 0.38 four colour set, black red green orange, 11.20, for the four marking roles; Uni Jetstream 0.38 black 2.50, fastest drying on cheap paper; Uni Kuru Toga Advance 0.5 pencil 8.50, lead rotates so the line stays even; Tombow MONO Zero 2.3 mm eraser 5.25 for precise corrections; Zebra Sarasa Mark On 0.4 red and blue 5.30. DO NOT BUY: more highlighters, the Mildliners already win; multi pens, slower than picking up a second pen; Zebra bLen, solves a problem you do not have.
